requirements.evidence: Data model and contracts are present: app/Models/Entity.php:18-51 (fillable, slug route key, memberships/users/owner), app/Models/UserRole.php:16-19, database/migrations/2026_10_29_073115_create_entity_memberships_table.php:21-27 (both unique indexes plus the portable stored-generated `owner_seq`), app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:15-62, routes/web.php:53-57 (auth+verified, exact paths/names), app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:71-95 (target must be another admin of this entity, owner row re-checked, roles swapped in a DB transaction), dashboard.blade.php:6-14 (settings link/owner notice only under `@can('manageSettings')`), and both lang files add `nav_members`/`nav_settings`/owner notice/transfer title. Remaining edge-case gaps: delete() is not atomic (Settings.php:61-62) and the 'last manager' guard in Members.php:88-94 can never fire because the owner is always counted and can never be removed.

conventions.evidence: Several clear deviations: domain writes are inline in the components rather than `app/Actions/*` (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:35-95, app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:31-97); Settings public properties have no `#[Validate]` attributes (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:20-24) although the project pattern is `#[Validate]` + `$this->validate()`; pick() authorises with a direct membership lookup instead of a policy (app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:32-36); views use almost no Bulma classes and extract no `<x-...>` components (resources/views/livewire/entity/*.blade.php). Migrations have reversible `down()` and models set `$fillable` deliberately (app/Models/Entity.php:18, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:22), so it is not a wholesale ignoring of the conventions.

security.evidence: Every Livewire action resolves the record scoped to the locked entity and authorises it server-side (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:64-66, 80-82; app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:37-39, 55-57, 73-75), the entity property is `#[Locked]` (Settings.php:17-18) so it cannot be swapped, all queries scope by `$this->entity->memberships()` so client IDs cannot reach another entity, and Blade uses `{{ }}` only. Gaps: no rate limiting on the sensitive delete/transfer actions (Settings.php:53-95), `$targetMembershipId` is neither validated nor locked (Settings.php:24, 76), and pick() bypasses the policy layer (EntityController.php:32-36). No exploitable flaw found.

tests.evidence: The diff creates no files under `tests/` at all: no model/factory tests, no policy tests, no `entity.pick` feature test, and no Livewire tests for the dashboard/members/settings actions (happy path, validation, unauthorized call, tamper). conventions.md requires 'No production code without a test' and an unauthorized-call plus tamper test for each action.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean: policies are reused via `$this->authorize`, the ownership swap is a single transaction, factories use states instead of bespoke builders, and no service/repository layer or speculative abstraction was added. Minor duplication: each Settings action re-fetches the entity with `Entity::findOrFail($this->entity->id)` and re-authorises (Settings.php:37-39, 55-57, 73-75), and there is no shared guard for the repeated 'owner row' abort.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are short and focused (Members.php:31-97, Settings.php:35-95); PHPDoc generics are added on models. Small blemishes: `User::entities()` is documented as `BelongsToMany<User, $this>` (app/Models/User.php:43-51), the duplicate-member error reuses the raw `validation.unique` template (Members.php:42), and the members view prints `role->value` raw and renders buttons that always 403 for the owner row/employees (members.blade.php:14-17).

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff serves the task: models/policies/migrations/factories, the pick action and routes, the three Livewire pages and their views, lang keys, plus the required docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG updates. No onboarding, switcher, middleware or unrelated refactor is included.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, so none of the new models, policies, migration constraints, routes or Livewire actions are covered, including the mandatory unauthorized-call and tamper tests.
Domain writes (save/delete/transfer, addMember/assignRole/removeMember) are performed inline in the Livewire components instead of the project's `app/Actions/*` one-class-per-use-case pattern.
`$name`, `$slug` and `$targetMembershipId` have no `#[Validate]` rules and `transfer()` never validates its target, deviating from the project's `#[Validate]` + `$this->validate()` pattern.
pick() authorises via a direct `membershipFor()` check instead of the `EntityPolicy::view` gate, bypassing the policy layer that conventions require for authorization.

The sensitive delete and ownership-transfer actions are not rate-limited, and an empty or tampered `targetMembershipId` produces a 403 instead of a validation error (only the scoped lookup prevents abuse).
delete() removes the memberships and then the entity outside a transaction, so a failure between the two calls leaves memberships permanently deleted while the entity survives.
The members list renders assign/remove buttons for the owner row and for employees, which always answer 403, and prints the raw `role->value` instead of a translated label.
The `entities()` relation is documented as `BelongsToMany<User, $this>` although it relates `Entity`.
The duplicate-member error reuses the raw `validation.unique` message template instead of adding a proper error for the `email` field.
Forms are bare inputs/buttons without Bulma classes and without extracting reusable markup into Blade components, contrary to the Bulma/UI conventions.
The ER diagram also drops the planned `entities.locale_default` column, an edit unrelated to the entity schema required by this task.

review.summary: The change implements the entity data model, the portable DB-level single-owner constraint, the policies, the pick route with audit logging, and the Livewire dashboard/members/settings pages, mostly matching the task contract and with sound scoped, policy-checked actions. It ships no tests whatsoever, which alone blocks merging, and it skips several project conventions (Actions for domain writes, `#[Validate]` attributes, policy-based authorization in the picker, Bulma/Blade components). The production code itself is a reasonable, secure implementation and mainly needs tests plus those convention fixes.
